transcript.text: hoover washer drier showing EO3 wont drain, ive done the filter its clean. H3DS4965DACE. pump just buzzes. do i need a new pump??

Based on the symptoms you've described—specifically that the pump buzzes but does not spin or drain—the short answer is: Yes, it is highly likely that you need to replace the pump.

Here’s a breakdown of why this is the case and what else you should check before buying parts.

### Why the Pump Buzzing Points to Failure
• Buzzing means power is reaching the pump: The fact that it buzzes tells us the control board is sending electricity to the pump motor, so the issue isn’t a faulty wiring harness or main PCB (at least not in the output stage).
• Buzzing without spinning = Mechanical Jam or Burnt Motor: A healthy drain pump should spin silently. If it’s buzzing:
    1.  Debris is jamming the impeller: Even if the filter is clean, small objects (coins, buttons, bra wires) can get lodged behind the filter in the pump housing itself, preventing the impeller from turning.
    2.  The pump motor has burned out internally: The windings may be shorted or the bearings are seized. This is very common on Hoover washer-driers after a few years of use.

### Steps to Confirm Before Replacing

1.  Check for Debris in the Pump Housing:
• Since you’ve already cleaned the filter, remove the pump entirely (you’ll need a screwdriver and possibly pliers).
• Look inside the pump inlet and outlet ports. Shine a torch into it. Try to spin the impeller blades by hand with your finger or tweezers.
• If it doesn’t spin freely or feels gritty/stuck, clear any debris. If it spins freely but still buzzes when powered, the motor is dead.

2.  Check for a Blocked Drain Hose:
• Ensure the drain hose isn’t kinked or clogged further down (e.g., in your home’s waste pipe). A severe blockage can sometimes cause the pump to struggle and overheat/buzz, though this usually triggers an error code quickly rather than just buzzing indefinitely.

3.  Inspect the Pump Impeller:
• When you remove the pump, check if the plastic impeller is cracked or broken. If it’s shattered, debris may have jammed it, but also replacing a damaged impeller requires a new pump anyway.

### Part Number for Your Model
Your model number is H3DS4965DACE. This is part of Hoover’s Direct Drive series (often rebadged as Indesit or Ariston).

• The drain pump for this model is typically a 12V DC pump.
• Common replacement part numbers include:
• C00324768
• C00324769 (check compatibility, as some variants differ slightly)
• 1150000000 or similar OEM-style numbers.

> ✅ Recommendation: Search for "Hoover H3DS drain pump" on eBay, Amazon, or appliance parts sites like PartSelect or ClickSpares. Enter your full model number (H3DS4965DACE) to confirm fitment. Most of these pumps cost between £20–£40.

### Installation Tips
• Unplug the machine before starting.
• Take a photo of the pump wiring and hose connections before disconnecting them.
• The pump is usually held in by 3–4 screws or clips. It’s often accessible from the back panel (you may need to remove the rear cover).
• When installing the new pump, ensure the O-ring/seal is properly seated to avoid leaks.

### If the New Pump Doesn’t Fix It
If you replace the pump and it still buzzes or doesn’t drain:
1.  Check the pressure switch/hose: A blocked pressure hose can confuse the machine into thinking water is still present, but this usually causes different error codes (like E04/E05 for filling issues).
2.  Main Control Board: In rare cases, if the new pump also buzzes immediately upon power-up without spinning, the control board’s relay or triac may be faulty, sending erratic voltage to the pump. However, this is far less common than a failed pump.

Verdict: Replace the drain pump first. It’s the most likely culprit and the easiest/cheapest fix.

ive already pulled the filter and turned the impeller with my finger, spins totally freely, no resistance at all, feels like its not connected to the motor. torch shows one fin looks snapped. meter on the coil reads about 170 ohms. so pump needs replacing right? is the pump a separate part from the filter housing on this model?

Yes, based on your findings—specifically the snapped impeller fin and the fact that it spins freely without resistance—the pump motor is definitely faulty. The snapped fin means the plastic impeller has detached from the magnetic rotor inside the motor, so even though the motor might still have some electrical continuity (170 ohms), it cannot physically move water.

### Is the Pump Separate from the Filter Housing?
On most Hoover washer-driers with model number H3DS4965DACE (which appears to be a Hoover H-Wash 140 or similar series), the drain pump is typically:

✅ A separate component that mounts onto the bottom of the filter housing.
❌ It is not usually sold as part of the filter assembly itself.

You will likely need to order just the drain pump, not the entire filter housing.

---

### Recommended Replacement Pump
For your model, you’ll want a pump that matches these specs:
• Voltage: 230V AC
• Frequency: 50Hz
• Resistance: ~170–200 ohms (yours is within range)
• Flow Rate: Typically around 4,000–5,000 L/h for washer-driers
• Mounting: Look for a pump with the same connector type and screw pattern.

Common replacement part numbers for this type of Hoover include:
• Whirlpool/Ariston-style drain pump (Hoover uses Whirlpool-group components)
• Part number examples: `480165`, `480172`, or `480193` — but always verify with your exact model.

### How to Replace It
1. Unplug the machine.
2. Tilt it back carefully (have someone help if possible) so you can access the bottom.
3. Remove the filter cover and unscrew the pump from the filter housing.
4. Disconnect the electrical plug and hose clamps.
5. Install the new pump, reconnect hoses and wiring, and reassemble.

### Where to Buy
• PartFinder.co.uk or Spares2go.com: Enter your full model number (`H3DS4965DACE`) to find the exact pump.
• Look for “Hoover H-Wash 140 drain pump” or similar.
